title: Sequential emission profile and backpressure notes
content:
Summary:

Quick notes from a sequence of trace-driven investigations into long-tail response latency caused around sequential emission and downstream backpressure. Goal: identify reproducible cohorts responsible for p95/p99 tails, enumerate stage-level contributors, and list low-effort mitigations to validate in canary.

Top-level findings (short):
- p50 is stable (~120ms) for typical prompt lengths (<=128 tokens). p95 jumps mostly from emitter stalls and network egress waits; p99 dominated by KV-cache miss cascades + batching handoff contention.
- Two distinct tail phenotypes observed: (A) slow-first-token during cold KV miss + model quantization kernel fallback, (B) intermittent emit stalls when downstream egress/backpressure causes token-emit backlog.
- Simple mitigations (async emit buffer + KV-prefetch for pinned models) reduce sampled p95 by ~18% in internal bench.

Representative metrics (sample window: 2025-09-01 to 2025-09-10, host: ded-gpu-a1):
- Overall (all routes): p50=118ms, p95=540ms, p99=1420ms
- Cohort: seqlen<=64: p50=95ms, p95=320ms, p99=720ms
- Cohort: seqlen 65-256: p50=160ms, p95=620ms, p99=1600ms
- Cold-start traces (KV miss on first request): p50=210ms, p95=820ms, p99=2400ms

Stage breakdown (aggregated by token emit; percent is of total token latency):
- Request ingress / auth: 2-4% (15-30ms typical)
- Tokenization / prompt preprocessing: 5-8% (20-60ms, grows with prompt)
- KV lookup / prefix-cache: 12-28% (cache-hit ~25ms, miss path includes disk or remote: 150-900ms)
- Attention + model forward kernels: 40-55% (dominant for large seqlen and large context; p99 affected by kernel fallback)
- Emit pipeline (formatting, safety check, serializer): 6-18% (unstable — big variance when backpressure present)
- Egress (socket flush, HTTP/stream backpressure): 4-22% (large when client-side read is slow)

Observed tail mechanisms (detailed):
1) KV miss cascade:
   - Trigger: unpinned model variant + prefix not present in LRU cache after autoscaler movement or pod restart.
   - Trace signature: long blocking call in stage "kv_fetch_remote" followed rapidly by increased attention time (due to deserializing weights/quant tables) and then an emit spike.
   - Triage notes: correlate with allocation events and node reboots; also matches periods with high eviction rate.

2) Emit backpressure / socket stalls:
   - Trigger: client reading slowly (e.g., browser with intermittent connectivity) or downstream proxy impose TLS renegotiation; also seen when concurrent streaming consumers exceed per-connection quotas.
   - Trace signature: repeated "emit_write_blocked" events in the last 1-2 tokens; CPU idle while awaiting socket write completion.
   - Impact: token emission latency multiplies across subsequent tokens until buffer drains; causes long p99 but p50 unaffected.

3) Kernel fallback at high sequence lengths:
   - Trigger: sequence length crosses threshold where optimized fused-attention kernel not supported (model shape mismatch or unsupported quant layout).
   - Trace signature: single token where "kernel_select" shows fallback and "compute_ms" spikes; subsequent tokens slower until kernel switch resets.

Sampling/Tracing methodology notes:
- Collected full-span traces with token-level spans (emit, kv, compute, egress). Sampling ratio 1:25 for production traffic; 1:1 for canary runs.
- Use trace tags: route_id, model_variant, pod_id, seq_len, kv_cache_hit. These are critical for cohort slicing.
- When analyzing p99, prioritize traces with seq_len>128 and kv_cache_hit=false.

Example exemplar trace (abridged):
[TRACE] id=trc-7f3a seq_len=192 model=redwood-v2-q4 pod=ded-gpu-a1 route=chatS1
  ingress_ms=12
  tokenize_ms=42
  kv_fetch_ms=842 (remote fetch)
  weight_deserialize_ms=95
  compute_ms=220
  emit_pipeline_ms=54
  emit_write_blocked_ms=560
  egress_flush_ms=95
  total_ms=1920
Notes: kv_fetch remote + socket write blocked combine to make p99.

Hypotheses and experiments to run (prioritized):
- H1: Pre-warming/pinning heavy-used model variants in Dedicated pools will reduce KV misses and p99. Experiment: add TTL-based pin for top 5 model variants + 24h prewarm job. Measure p99 delta over 24h.
- H2: Allow async emitter buffer with backpressure signaling to model runtime so compute can continue while emit drains. Experiment: enable emitter_buffer=64 tokens in canary. Watch memory and net saturation.
- H3: Introduce fast path fallback telemetry: when kernel_select chooses fallback, inject small warm-up micro-batch to re-trigger optimized kernel. Experiment: kernel_warm_probe toggle on canary builds.

Playbook for immediate mitigations (canary-friendly):
- Set kv_cache_retention higher for routes where p99 >> p95 and requests are bursty (temporary 2x).
- Configure emitter_buffer and enable per-connection flow-control metrics to detect sustained backpressure and proactively increase buffer for that connection (safeguard: cap total extra memory to avoid OOM).
- Adjust batcher max_wait_ms for high-seqlen routes to favor smaller batches (reduces contention on compute kernels that scale poorly with heterogeneous seq_len).

Data slices to present to PM / SRE for rollouts:
- Time-series: p50/p95/p99 by route, overlaid with kv_eviction_rate and node_restarts.
- Heatmap: emit_write_blocked_count vs client-region (to detect problematic ISPs/proxies).
- Cohort table: (route, seq_len_bucket, kv_hit_rate, p95, p99, top_stage).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need root-cause link for a cluster event on 2025-08-28 that shows coincident KV eviction spike; ticket JIRA-1248 opened (linked).
- Measure memory vs latency tradeoff when using larger emitter buffers under normal concurrency (risk: memory amplification under high QPS).
- Is there an opportunity for adaptive quant-kernel selection that avoids full fallback cost? Follow-up with research (Lin).

Immediate action items (owners):
- Aisha: spin up 1-day canary with emitter_buffer=64 and kv_cache_retention=2x for route=chatS1; collect 1:1 traces and prepare p95/p99 comparison (due: 2025-09-18).
- Miguel: add trace tag kv_eviction_reason to the kv_fetch span and correlate with autoscaler logs (due: 2025-09-15).
- Lin: prototype kernel_warm_probe and run microbench for seq_len 128/256 to measure warm-up cost (due: 2025-09-22).

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally rough; it's a synthesis of trace samples and bench runs. The goal is to get actionable canary changes out quickly. Expect follow-ups with consolidated dashboards and a short playbook if mitigations reduce p99 by >15%.

Appendix: quick grep-friendly trace tags to filter in the trace viewer:
- "kv_fetch_ms>200"  -> finds cache miss cascades
- "emit_write_blocked_count>0"  -> finds backpressure-affected traces
- "kernel_select=fallback"  -> finds kernel fallback cases

End of notes.
